bodies: Here is a two by two matrix. Four little numbers, and they look harmless. But a matrix is not a table. It is a machine that grabs space and stretches it.
Watch. Start with a unit square, area one. Feed it to the machine. The square leans over into a parallelogram, and the new area is three. That three is the determinant.
So when your textbook says a d minus b c, it is not being cryptic. Two times two, minus one times one, leaves three. The same three. It is just the stretch factor.
But when the determinant hits zero, space does not stretch. It flattens. The square is crushed onto a line, and nothing you do will ever get it back.
